title: Audit-family critique: which are load-bearing, and what the staleness metric actually measures
description: Filed as P8 during the W4 gate ("needs Jordan's call on which audit families are load-bearing"); this is the evidence for that call. Document: audit/2026-07-30-audit-family-critique/00_critique.md. HEADLINE. The vector audit IS the thing that identifies what is missing and nothing else in the repo computes it, AND its findings are near-stationary. Both are true at once and the staleness metric conflates them. MEASURED: over 8 days and 240 files of in-scope churn the feed moved 3 rows out of 178, in the improving direction (isolates 9->7, sparse_context 16->15; implied_missing 35 and notional 100 byte-stable). A freshness warning on a stationary backlog measures the wrong axis -- it says 're-run a script' when the message should be '178 structural gaps have gone unworked'. RECOMMENDATION 1 is therefore to INVERT what it reports (backlog counts, not drift), NOT to demote it; an earlier draft of this analysis recommended demotion and that was wrong, for the reason the two-axis split in the document's section 1 gives (content value and staleness informativeness are uncorrelated here). PER-FAMILY: mechanics-index is the one to promote -- it has NO generator, so its drift is editorial debt no script can clear, and it is the smallest number on the banner. vector-audit is highest on content value, lowest on staleness informativeness (both production paths regenerate the feed immediately before consuming it). graph-lexicon is low on both. decisions/proposals/apparatus are the governance observatory, NOT part of the vectorization review at all -- only vector-audit (its output), graph-lexicon (soft input) and mechanics-index (cited input) touch skills/valoria-vector-audit/. npc-audit should be reclassified: its artifact is an AUTHORED document, so 'stale' means a human must re-audit, sharing no remedy with 're-run a script'. THREE METRIC DEFECTS. D1: drift is computed from the artifact's last git COMMIT, not its last regeneration, so a no-op regen commits nothing and drift accumulates forever while the artifact is provably current -- not firing today (regeneration does change content) but silent when it does. D2: the weekly cron is nominally weekly, actually 1-in-3 -- exactly ONE scheduled refresh has ever landed (4029870, PR #244, 2026-07-27), the only commit matching the bot's own message; vector-audit and graph-lexicon last moved 07-22 and were not updated by the 07-27 run. D3: scope over-breadth manufactures the headline -- vector-audit's scope is most of the repo, so 240 files of churn produced 3 changed rows; the code carries a prior correction for exactly this failure mode at a smaller scope. THREE OF THIS ANALYSIS'S OWN HYPOTHESES WERE WRONG and were corrected by reading rather than grepping: ci_naming_check does NOT consume lexicon.json (it EXCLUDES it, skip-list at :70); review_core does NOT read apparatus_registry.yaml (comment only, :52); and the graph.json-pinned CI drift guard described at vector_audit.py:1215-1222 NO LONGER EXISTS -- the guard was rewritten to remove the dependency, so that docstring is STALE (recorded, not fixed: it is a skills/ file and this was a read-only critique). title: Standing gate: an adversarial steelmanned read-only review after EVERY milestone, not at the end
description: RULED (Jordan, 2026-08-04): 'use Fable 5 after every milestone/step to do an adversarial steelman read-only review for accuracy and logic and fidelity to plan'. Recorded in systems/_architecture/repository_keep_set_v1.md section 7.1 as a gate on every step of the evacuation sequence: a step is not complete until the review has run and its findings are applied or explicitly refused with a reason. WHAT THIS ADDS TO EXISTING DOCTRINE. CLAUDE.md section 10 already requires the agonist->antagonist relay and already wires valoria-critic (Read/Grep/Glob only, so independence is structural rather than declared, ED-IN-0087). It does NOT specify a CADENCE. This does: per MILESTONE, not per programme. JUSTIFIED FROM THIS PROGRAMME'S OWN RECORD, not from principle. Three defects in the separation work were found by adversarial passes and by nothing else, each invisible to the instrument that had just been built and pronounced sound: (1) the contest-groundup parity oracle sat in the evacuate set while a kept tool loads it to regenerate a committed golden a kept CI test asserts on (ED-IN-0130); (2) readers() could not see split paths, so the blocking-reader counts that sequence the entire deletion were blind to os.path.join construction -- 45 readers missed (ED-IN-0130); (3) deprecated/ holds 26 files of the BLOCKING ED-citation gate's universe, so the evacuation commit would have turned that gate red and the tempting fix would have destroyed the repo's only anti-fabrication check (ED-IN-0131). Each was cheap to check and expensive to have acted on. A single end-of-programme review would have caught all three AFTER the work they invalidate. THREE PROPERTIES THE GATE MUST KEEP or it decays into ceremony: (a) read-only BY CONSTRUCTION -- route through valoria-critic, never a prompt that merely declares read-only, since a sentence inside a prompt restricts nothing; (b) STEELMAN FIRST -- the reviewer states the strongest case for the work before attacking it, and 'this is correct and here is the best argument for it' is a valid verdict; (c) THE REVIEWER'S CLAIMS ARE CHECKED TOO -- reviews have been wrong in this programme (one reported id_reservations next_free unbumped when it was bumped; it had read a mid-session snapshot), so an audit is evidence, not a verdict. NOT YET ENFORCED. This is a convention with no guard. A CI check cannot observe whether a review ran, so the honest options are a per-step artifact under audit/ or a required line in the step's commit message. Filed rather than asserted -- per CLAUDE.md 0.1 point 5, if the guard cannot be written the pattern is not yet understood, and I am not claiming enforcement I have not built.

description: W4a of the separation work list (HANDOFF_IN). The clearest data-in-prose violation in the tree, named as 'the clearest inversion' by the fork plan §4.1 and unexecuted until now. WHAT LANDED. tools/export_key_types.py cooks the markdown to engine/engine_params/key_types.json, following the established typed-export convention (_generated header, schema_version, source, --check round-trip). title: W4a gate response: load_json was a WEAKER validator than the markdown path, and I re-committed the stale-quotation defect inside the docstring that lectures about it
description: Response to the ED-IN-0132 gate review of W4a (verdict COMPLETE-WITH-RESIDUALS). The MARKDOWN path gets two guarantees structurally for free: the heading regex [a-z_]+.[a-z_]+ makes a malformed type id UNREPRESENTABLE, and _parse_entry always returns a dict. So the JSON path was strictly weaker than the path it is replacing. PROVEN, not argued: {'types': {'NotAnId': 42}} LOADED. Tolerable while echo_transport is the only consumer of a CI-pinned file; not tolerable when W4b binds three more consumers and W4c binds Godot -- a weaker validator on the path that is BECOMING PRIMARY is the wrong direction. Fixed to parity: type-id shape (sharing a compiled pattern with the heading regex so the two loaders cannot disagree about what a valid id is), entry-is-dict, and a type_count cross-check that uses the count the document already carries instead of letting it rot unread. The fix is not 'be careful': it is that prose about code must DESCRIBE or cite something that does not shift. Line numbers in a file that is being edited are a self-inflicted staleness generator, and quoting a file you are changing in the same commit is guaranteed to be wrong. title: engine/params/ flips KEEP -> EVACUATE: the 43 parameter-table .md captured byte-lossless into YAML first; and the slice report's first sub-root evacuation exposed two false-positive scans
description: Jordan, 2026-08-04: 'params .md are largely useless at this point and I want them gone. code should have superseded them all by now' / 'just dump the constants to a yaml' / 'provenance can cite to a fork'. evacuation_plan.py's R-PARAMS-INFO rule said KEEP ('prose WITH a code pair -> information only'), justified by ~50 provenance referents from kept code that a deletion would orphan; the fork-citation ruling dissolves that objection, so the rule is now R-PARAMS-DUMPED (evacuate). WHAT WAS NOT ASSUMED. The census that motivated this -- 295 of 378 ALL-CAPS identifiers found in code (78%) -- is an OPTIMISTIC UPPER BOUND and its residue was noise (capitalised prose ALIGNMENT/DISTILLED, HTML markers AUD1, character names ALDRIC/MARET); a name appearing in code never proved its VALUE matched. So the deletion is NOT gated on that measurement. tools/export_params_constants.py captures the tables structurally (file -> section -> header + rows, cells verbatim, no invented schema -- typing them would be authorship) AND stores every file's full text in a `raw` map, making the capture lossless BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by my parser being total. It is not: six files (index stubs, history/) yield no table at all, which is exactly how a silent loss would have happened. Measured: 43/43 files captured, every one byte-identical to source, 258 tables, 1367 rows. THE GATE IS DELIBERATELY TEMPORARY. `--check` re-derives from engine/params/, so it cannot survive its own source; it is wired blocking in all four places (valoria-ci.yml, valoria_local.py, ci_checks_registry.yaml, test_gate_coverage.EXPECTED_COMMANDS -- the exact four-way omission that caused the ED-IN-0137 regression) and must be retired in the SAME commit that deletes engine/params/. No vacuous-pass-on-absent-source path exists, so forgetting turns CI loudly red rather than quietly green. TWO SCAN DEFECTS THE FLIP EXPOSED, both false-positive classes that would have made the deletion report unreadable. (1) engine/ is the FIRST root that only partly evacuates; readers() scanned kept files for the top-level directory, so a 43-file slice reported 'engine/' hits across nearly the whole tree. Fixed with slice_prefixes(): a slice is the shortest prefix under which NOTHING is retained. This also retroactively tightens tests/ and deprecated/, which had the same looseness. (2) joined_path_readers() counted a constructed path as a breakage if ANYTHING under it evacuated; tests/sim holds both evacuating stress prose and the KEPT canon mass-battle engine, so all 30 kept readers of the canon engine were reported as silent breakages. Now requires the target to be WHOLLY evacuating. Split-path alarms fell 33 -> 4, and the four remaining are real. RESULT (re-measured post-commit, when the 3 new files are tracked): 3153 tracked -> 1653 keep + 33 relocate = 1686 retained / 1467 evacuate. The pre-flip figure was 1693 keep + 33 relocate = 1726 retained, so the flip moves 43 files and the 3 new tool/test/data files return 3. CORRECTION (gate review F5): the first version of this entry wrote '1683 keep (was 1650)', comparing keep+relocate against keep-only -- an apples-to-oranges aside, and the kind of unreconciled number this ledger exists to stop. The headline share is unaffected: markdown share of the retained tree 51.9% -> 50.6%. The params tree was a small dent; audit/ (493 kept .md across 59 units, under Jordan's July rule) is 58% of all retained markdown and is the only remaining lever worth more than a percentage point. GATE REVIEW RESPONSE (ED-IN-0132 pass, verdict COMPLETE-WITH-RESIDUALS; fixes landed in the follow-up commit). F1 THE HEADLINE CLAIM WAS UNGUARDED: the exporter read text-mode with errors='ignore' and the falsifier verified with the IDENTICAL lossy read, so a CRLF line or an undecodable byte would be normalised/dropped on both sides and the pair would agree with each other while diverging from the file -- two lossy reads that match are not evidence of losslessness. Now reads bytes and decodes strictly (an invalid byte raises rather than vanishing) and the test compares raw bytes against the capture re-encoded. Measured: zero CR bytes across the 43 files, so the dump is byte-unchanged; what changed is what happens to a file that arrives before the deletion slice. F2 SCOPE GAP: the rule evacuates engine/params/** while the capture globbed **/*.md AND the test used the same filter -- guard and capture shared a blind spot (glob also skips dotfiles). Both now walk the tree; the exporter refuses to write if any file is outside the capture glob. Empty today, which is luck, not design. F3 THE CONTROL COVERED ONLY THE COMPLETENESS BRANCH -- it planted an omission, not a mismatch, so the byte comparison carrying the word 'byte-identical' had no falsifier at all, and this entry described the control as stronger than it was. Four content mutations added (cell delimiter, trailing newline, LF->CRLF, one digit). F4 a stale '1,996 files' survived in test_evacuation_plan.py's docstring in the same commit that changed the count to 1467 -- the ED-IN-0134/0138 stale-quotation class again, now removed rather than restated. F6 CLAUDE.md 5 still taught engine/params/ as the live number surface and listed the typed round-trip-checked export as 'not yet built'; amended. F7 the local references/evacuation_manifest.json was stale but is gitignored and untracked -- regenerated. F8 the reviewer swept for true positives lost to the scan tightening and found none. NOT ACCEPTED AS DEFECTS: nothing; all six actionable findings were taken.

title: W3 deletion rehearsal: the shipping gate does not COLLECT after the cut — a third reader blind spot
description: Executed the partition in a throwaway worktree: 1,724 files deleted, 1,279 tracked. Four blocking gates broke, one predicted. Deleting it does not fail a test, it stops pytest COLLECTING AT ALL -- strictly worse than a red test and invisible to every static prediction. module_import_readers() added, TRANSITIVE (one hop was demonstrably wrong: keeping github_ops.py immediately made its two imports load-bearing), with a false positive killed before reporting (`import engine` resolves to the top-level PACKAGE). title: THE EVACUATION: 1,721 files removed, and the FORKED terminal status that let live citations survive it
description: Jordan: 'I don't really understand why we didn't just bulk move a whole bunch of stuff to fork, leave things dangling in main, and just resolve from there' -- then 'just fucking do it'. He was right. Three layers of reader-prediction machinery existed to FORECAST what a deletion would break; the W3 rehearsal answered it in ten minutes by doing it. Executed: 3,003 -> 1,282 tracked, evacuate set 1,721 -> 0. Recovery point c2e5bc8. UNBLOCKED BY: excising tools/compliance_check.py's orchestrator half (check_all / validate_commit / auto_fix / find_index_for / _lazy_import and the /home/claude sys.path insert). Its `import github_ops` was the LAST live reference from the non-deprecated tree into the retired orchestrator; the CI path never called any of it; removal cost ZERO live functionality. THE FORKED TERMINAL STATUS is the one piece of new mechanism and it was NOT optional: 25 live ledger entries cite audit units that were their EVIDENCE and are now at a fork ref. Every unresolvable reference was DEAD, so correct citations read as breakage in a blocking gate. A restructure_ledger row may now target FORK:<ref>, meaning legitimately absent with provenance at that ref. CRITICALLY it is NOT 'ignore missing' -- a reference with no row still fails -- because erasing that distinction would destroy the anti-fabrication property. A review named this as the single most likely thing to go wrong, so the control shipped WITH the status: tests/valoria/test_forked_status.py plants both cases, requires every FORK ref to be a real commit, and verifies the evacuated content is ACTUALLY present at that ref rather than trusting the row. GATES: 7 red -> 0. export_params_constants retired with its source from 5 wiring points; 8 completed one-shot .claude/wf_*.js retired with their subject (34 DEAD -> 0); ci_wf_harness_check taught that zero scripts is legitimate while still failing if the OWNER is missing; freshness_gate green by PRUNING canonical_sources (not --update, which would pin nothing for missing files and silently bless the deletion); currency_consistency_check taught that a tombstone line is not a head claim, line-locally so a genuinely stale head elsewhere still fails.

title: Post-evacuation cleanup: 24 test failures -> 0, by deleting what lost its subject rather than repairing it
description: Jordan: 'Keep it simple, ie don't build tools unnecessarily.' A read-only review triaged the 24 failures left by the evacuation and found ONE genuinely broken kept tool; everything else was a guard outliving the thing it guarded. Disposition was DELETE by default. DELETED, subject gone: tests/valoria/test_params_dump.py (7 failures -- it existed to make the engine/params deletion safe, and that deletion is now merged; a safety guard for a consumed one-way door guards nothing). tools/ci_formula_prose_check.py + its test + 4 wiring points -- BOTH its inputs left main (the census and its entire live-scan surface), so it was a report-only gate printing 'no drift' over nothing, which its own comment records having happened for 14 days once already. 46 dead LANE_PATH_PREFIXES rows in build_decisions -- a lane-map row matching nothing does not fail loudly, it silently leaves the lane unassigned. Two one-liners: build_proposals' ranked_view (linked at an evacuated doc -- a link nobody can follow is worse than no link) and engine/params/ from validate_ed_citations' scan prefixes. FIXED, genuinely broken: tools/build_identifier_census.py imported parse_file from the retired export_params_constants and ImportError'd on invocation. The 'one owner' deferral was correct when written; deferring to an owner whose subject then leaves makes the dependency the defect. Parser inlined, ~20 lines, no second consumer to drift against. TERMINAL-STATE TEST CASUALTIES, the interesting class: four tests asserted against a NON-EMPTY evacuate set, which is now empty -- the state the tool was built to reach. Asserting the scan finds something is asserting the job is unfinished. Rewritten to plant their own inputs, so the property (a mixed prefix is not evacuating; a constructed path into an evacuating tree is found) survives the success of the thing it was watching. Same shape for test_wf_harness_check, whose fixture COPIED a wf_*.js retired with the evacuation: all 20 tests errored at setup. Synthesising a donor from the owner block was tried and rejected on measurement -- the gate enforces per-script rules a minimal synthetic script fails -- so the last real donor was restored from the fork ref as a committed FIXTURE. Data, not tooling. CLAUDE.md section 3 corrected: it still described arcs/ as a live primary, audit/ as organised into lane buckets that no longer exist, and engine/params/ as 'deletion lands in W7'. The deprecated/ row now records what SURVIVES and why -- the editorial-ledger archives are the BLOCKING citation gate's ED universe, and removing them would destroy the anti-fabrication check.
